chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Amir, from Khattab ibn Maslama, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: O Fadl, indeed our Hadith revives the hearts.

key_terms.حَدِيثُنَا: Our Hadith (referring to the teachings of the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual effect of the Imams' Hadith on the heart?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) highlights the transformative spiritual efficacy of Ahl al-Bayt’s teachings, asserting that they do not merely inform but actively 'revive' the hearts, akin to rain reviving dead earth. This concept underscores the Shia belief in the living, dynamic nature of Imami tradition, where deep contemplation of their words leads to spiritual awakening and moral rectification. The metaphor connects intellectual reception with spiritual vitality, a key theme in Shia hermeneutics.
